input.claim_text: On 9 February 2024 I woke up to find someone had spray-painted graffiti all over our front fence and garage door overnight. It looks like it happened while we were asleep since there was nothing there when we went to bed. I haven't had anyone come out to quote on repainting or replacing the panels yet, so I don't have a cost figure at this stage.

output.cause: unknown person spray-painted graffiti on front fence and garage door overnight

input.query: Is vandalism / malicious damage graffiti to fences and garage doors covered?

output.answer:
Based on the excerpts provided, vandalism/malicious damage is covered under the policy, but the excerpts do not specifically address graffiti to fences and garage doors as a distinct category.

What the excerpts show:

- Malicious damage is covered: "Malicious Yes Covered as deliberate or intentional act (including vandalism and a malicious act) but not by You, Your Family or anyone who normally lives in Your Home including a tenant." [NRMA Home KFS, page 1]

- The PDS confirms: "We cover loss or damage by a deliberate or intentional act (including vandalism and a malicious act)." Cover applies to "Your Home if You have 'Building' insurance" and "Your General Contents while in Your Home if You have 'Contents' insurance." [NRMA Home PDS, page 13]

- Exclusions apply if the deliberate/intentional act (including vandalism) was committed by: You, Your Family, anyone who normally lives in Your Home (including a tenant), or anyone who enters with consent of You/Your Family/an occupant. [NRMA Home PDS, page 13]

- A condition of cover is that "You must report any deliberate or intentional act to the police and provide Us with the report number and details of when and where the report was made." [NRMA Home PDS, page 13]

Gap in the excerpts: There is no specific mention of "fences" or "garage doors" in relation to vandalism/graffiti cover, and no explicit statement on whether graffiti removal/cleaning is treated differently from other malicious damage. If fences are classified as part of "Your Home" (building) under this policy, the general vandalism cover described above would likely extend to them, but the excerpts do not confirm this definition, nor do they confirm whether graffita specifically (as opposed to physical damage) is covered.

**I cannot fully confirm coverage for graffiti to fences and garage doors specifically** — the excerpts do not contain a definition of "Home" that confirms fences/garage doors are included, nor do they address graffiti as a specific peril. You would need to consult the full PDS definitions section (e.g., "What is Your Home") to confirm this.
